prompt: Write a one-star review of the Eiffel Tower from an American who has seen the one in Las Vegas.
response:
One star. And I’m being generous.

Look, I don’t know who needs to hear this, but we have one of these back home in Las Vegas and, honestly, it’s just better. I booked this entire trip to Paris because my wife wanted the “authentic” experience, and what did we get? A rusty, cramped, overpriced disappointment.

First of all, no air conditioning. It’s 2024. The Vegas Eiffel Tower is inside a nice, climate-controlled casino. You take the elevator up, you’re not sweating through your polo. In Paris? I was packed into a lift like a sardine with 50 other tourists who apparently don’t believe in deodorant. The French call it “charm”; I call it a biohazard.

Second, the view. In Vegas, you look out and see the Bellagio fountains, the mountains, the strip—action. Excitement. Here, it’s just a bunch of beige buildings and a river that looks like chocolate milk. They didn’t even have the decency to put a bathroom up there. My kid had to go, and the attendant just shrugged and said “en bas” (downstairs). At the top of the Stratosphere, you can actually do things, like ride a roller coaster. This is just a glorified radio antenna with a gift shop.

And the light show? Vegas has a choreographed LED spectacular every night. This place just flickers for five minutes like a defective string of Christmas lights. My neighbor’s Halloween display has better tech.

Save your $30 and the 14-hour flight. Just go to the Paris casino, get a yard-long margarita, and ride the elevator to the top of the fake one. It’s cleaner, it’s cooler, and nobody tries to sell you a tiny, wobbly keychain of the very thing you’re standing on. Huge letdown.
